newsitem.title: UK: Sleepy Kids lower U.S. revenues hit profits.
newsitem.headline: Sleepy Kids lower U.S. revenues hit profits.

text.p: Sleepy Kids Plc said in a statement that lower revenues from the U.S. will hit group pretax profits in the current reporting period, covering 14 months to the end of 1996.
But it said it was "too early to quantify the degree to which profits have been effected."
Sleepy Kids said it made the statement in response to share price movements. The share was four pence lower at 22-1/2 pence by 1520 GMT today.
The company added that it was possible that other properties which it owned and projects it is working on "could make a satisfactory contribution to group revenues in the current year."
Sleepy Kids said it felt the share price fall reflected concerns over U.S. performance of its Budgie the Little Helicopter interests aimed at children.

It said Budgie the Little Helicopter, the children's storybook character created by Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of Britain's Prince Andrew, had not performed as expected in the U.S. because of delays in introduction of a merchandising programme.

Sleepy Kids said "important momentum was lost" as a result and the agent responsible for Budgie's marketing in the U.S., Launey Hachmann Harris Inc, filed for bankruptcy protection in April and its relationship with Sleepy Kids ended.
"There will be a necessary legal delay until a new U.S. agent can be appointed, but then the property will be relaunched throughout the U.S. via a stronger agent," Sleepy Kids said.
Sleepy Kids said FCN, which had been broadcasting Budgie, changed the format of scheduling and discontinued its Fox Cubhouse programme which included Budgie.
But it said ratings quoted by FCN "were regarded as very successful and the Budgie series was one of the highest-rated performers in the Fox Cubhouse programme."

Rights licensed originally to FCN will revert back to Sleepy Kids if FCN do not buy a fourth series by March 1997, although FCN president Margaret Loesch has said it intends to show a series of Budgie specials throughout 1996/97 season.
Sleepy Kids said in the UK it was discussing a fourth series for 1998 of Budgie with the ITV Network Centre, via its co-producer HTV.
"Ratings for the repeat of the second series...were extremely high," the company said.
Sleepy Kids said it was currently in talks for a U.S. home video deal on Budgie and has signed a publishing deal with Simon & Schuster in the U.S. for further books.
"It is very frustrating to have such a success on coast-to-coast U.S. television, only for it to be wasted by missed opportunities," said chairman Martin Powell.
He said it was a temporary setback which would slow Budgie's U.S. growth this year.
"I would like to emphasise that Sleepy Kids is not solely dependent upon this or any other individual property," he added.
